faqs.q: Can you get a raccoon family out of a Manassas chimney?
faqs.a: Yes — spring raccoon mothers in Manassas often pick an uncapped chimney or a soffit corner to raise young. Virginia prohibits trap-and-relocate, so our crew works under a Commercial Nuisance Animal Permit: the family is removed or evicted at the structure, any release happens on the property itself, and we finish by fitting a proper chimney cap and sealing the entry so the next raccoon cannot use it.

Manassas.wildlife_intro:
Manassas is an independent city inside Prince William County's area — older downtown homes plus postwar suburbs in Manassas. Our crew's calls here follow the ground: bull Run at the city's edge, historic downtown, Manassas Battlefield just outside the city. Raccoons and gray squirrels take attics and chimneys, striped skunks and opossums work yards and crawlspaces, and bats settle older rooflines in summer.

In spring we remove denning raccoon and squirrel families before the young are mobile. Summer brings skunk, groundhog, and snake calls and the bat maternity season, when exclusion waits under Virginia permit conditions. Fall is sealing season in Manassas — squirrels, rats, and bats all test the same gaps looking for winter shelter, and our crew closes them after the animals are out, because sealing alone rarely holds.
